newsitem.title: USA: U.S. offers to host Mideast summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers to host Mideast summit.

text.p: The United States is offering to host a summit in Washington between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, a senior administration official said on Saturday.
"This is something we are talking to the parties about," the official said of the possibility of hosting a meeting. "It's one of several ideas that have been presented," he added.

The senior official, who was travelling with President Bill Clinton on a campaign trip, said "there are still a lot of factors that have not been nailed down ... at this point, no decision has been made."

"We have no meeting to announce but a lot of work has gone into it." Secretary of State Warren Christopher has led what was described as "intense efforts" to defuse the latest crisis, which threatens to unravel peace efforts in the region.
Officials in Washington said mediators were working on a seven-point plan to defuse the crisis, based around a meeting soon between Arafat and Netanyahu.
The sources said efforts were under way to set up a meeting between Arafat and Netanyahu, most likely somewhere in the Middle East. After that, they would go to Washington and join Clinton.
In the West Bank and Gaza, Palestinian police kept a lid on protests on Saturday, after four days of violent protests that claimed nearly 70 lives.

It would be a politically risky move for Clinton to bring the two Mideast leaders to Washington before the Nov. 5 election. Although such a summit could enhance the president's stature as a world statesman, it also would plunge him personally into the middle of one of the world's most intractable problems.

Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole, in Florida, was asked about his views on the current tensions between Israel and the Palestinians. "I hope they get together today and start talking," he replied.

Palestinian police in riot gear stopped hundreds of youths on Saturday from marching on an Israeli checkpoint at Ramallah, north of Jerusalem, scene of some of the fiercest fighting in the past four days.
They also thwarted protests in the West Bank town of Qalqilya and at Rafah in the Gaza Strip, witnesses said.

U.S. Consul General in Jerusalem Edward Abington met Arafat in Gaza, urging him to meet Netanyahu. Terje Larsen, the U.N. coordinator in Gaza, also met Arafat and Netanyahu on Saturday to work on the seven-point framework, diplomatic sources said.
Netanyahu's spokesman, Shai Bazak, said the Israeli leader was ready in principle to meet Arafat.
